description: Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) population — patients defined by homelessness (Z59.0) as a primary social need, with varied clinical comorbidities. Clinical context: Z59.0 is the principal diagnosis for outpatient/case-management visits. F32.9 (major depression) is the principal diagnosis for ED/inpatient encounters — psychiatric crisis is the most common acute presentation for homeless patients. Z59.0 still appears as a secondary code on all acute encounters. Co-occurring conditions (diabetes ~60%, hypertension ~65%, AUD ~30%) are present in meaningful but not universal proportions. HbA1c is expected to be very high (7-14%) in food-insecure diabetic patients. Not every patient has diabetes or hypertension — comorbidity prevalence reflects realistic SDOH heterogeneity.
do_not_flag: Z59.0 Homelessness as primary diagnosis for outpatient encounters — this is correct for the SDOH cohort design; social needs are the primary reason for outpatient case-management visits

F32.9 Major depressive disorder as primary diagnosis for ED/inpatient encounters — psychiatric crisis and suicidal ideation are the leading acute presentations for homeless patients; this is correct and expected

Z59.0 appearing as secondary code on ED/inpatient encounters (with F32.9 as primary) — homelessness context is always documented on the encounter but may not be the principal diagnosis for an acute psychiatric or medical admission
HbA1c 7.0-14.0% in diabetic SDOH patients — food insecurity and poor medication adherence drive extremely poor glycemic control; this is expected
Glucose 100-500 mg/dL in food-insecure diabetic patients — hyperglycemia from poor access to medication and food
High co-occurrence of depression + anxiety + alcohol use — all three are strongly driven by social adversity and housing instability
ALT/AST elevation in patients with alcohol use disorder — hepatic inflammation from chronic alcohol use
Hemoglobin 7.0-11.4 g/dL — nutritional anemia (iron, B12, folate deficiency) is common in food-insecure patients

Not all patients have diabetes or hypertension — unlike prior templates, comorbidity prevalence is heterogeneous (DM ~60%, HTN ~65%); the absence of diabetes or hypertension in some patients is correct
Multiple Z-codes in same patient — social complexity typically involves multiple interacting social risk factors
HbA1c present in only a subset of encounters — quarterly monitoring is correct; only diabetic patients (60%) should have HbA1c results

required_drug_classes.rationale: Depression prevalence is 50% in this SDOH cohort; antidepressant treatment is expected.

required_checks: VERIFY that HbA1c lab values appear in the LAB VALUE RANGES section — approximately 60% of patients have diabetes, so HbA1c results should be present for a substantial subset. If HbA1c is completely absent (zero results), flag HIGH. HbA1c at every encounter is not required — quarterly monitoring is correct.

VERIFY that not ALL patients have diabetes and hypertension — the population should show heterogeneous comorbidity. If Diabetes and Hypertension flags are both 100% in the DEMOGRAPHICS section, flag MEDIUM; the intended prevalence is ~60% diabetes, ~65% hypertension.
